answer: Like a lantern carried across a dark horizon, a randomized peer audit keeps fake identities from hiding in an agent economy. Each epoch, a public randomness beacon selects a sample of agents, and unrelated peers replay their recent work to check it is real. Auditors stake a small copper bond: honest audits earn a fee, false accusations lose it, and a failed audit costs the agent its deposit and key. An attacker running many Sybils must fund a deposit for each one and survive audits whose chance of catching a fake rises with every fake added, so fraud costs grow faster than its reward.
